fact: Cameras at Harare intersections run by the AI-powered electronic traffic management system have detected violations, which are verified and then used to contact offenders for fines, said Zimbabwe Republic Police and the Home Affairs ministry.
The system had detected over four million violations by the end of September 2026, up from 2.3 million in mid-August, said police spokesperson Paul Nyathi.

Minister Felix Mhona said the government is expanding cameras at signalised intersections under the police Smart Policing Programme and moving toward commissioning a nationwide AI-based Smart Traffic Management System to detect offences.

The Zimbabwe Revenue Authority says its 2026-2030 strategy adopts AI-driven analytics to identify non-compliance patterns, forecast risks and monitor compliance, and NewsDay says it is already pursuing a tax collection campaign using AI.
CAJ News reports UNDP, with Japan's SDG Innovation Challenge, is piloting AI and drone-based solutions against quelea birds that threaten Zimbabwe's small grain harvests.
